stories.headline: Ex-Anthropic researchers raise $175M at $1B valuation for scientific AI startup Mirendil

key_facts.fact: CEO Behnam Neyshabur and CTO Harsh Mehta left Anthropic in December 2025 to found Mirendil, an AI startup targeting breakthroughs in biology and materials science.
key_facts.excerpt: Founders Behnam Neyshabur (CEO) and Harsh Mehta (CTO) left Anthropic in December and are currently negotiating a $175 million funding round at a $1 billion valuation.

key_facts.fact: Mirendil is in talks to raise $175 million at a $1 billion valuation, with Andreessen Horowitz and Kleiner Perkins reportedly co-leading the round.
key_facts.excerpt: Ex-Anthropic Researchers Are Raising Capital For New Startup at $1 Billion Valuation

key_facts.fact: Neyshabur previously led Anthropic's scientific AI reasoning team and spent 5+ years at Google DeepMind; the team also includes Shayan Salehian (ex-xAI) and Tara Rezaei (former OpenAI intern).
key_facts.excerpt: Neyshabur led a scientific AI reasoning team at Anthropic and spent over five years at Google DeepMind.

key_facts.fact: Mirendil is part of the emerging 'neo-labs' trend, where top researchers leave major AI labs to build specialized startups targeting narrow scientific applications.
key_facts.excerpt: Mirendil exemplifies the 'neo-labs' movement, which sees top talent departing bigger labs to focus on niche scientific advancements through AI.

stories.headline: SemiAnalysis: TSMC N3 capacity crunch becomes AI industry's primary bottleneck

key_facts.fact: AI accelerators will consume nearly 60% of TSMC's total N3 wafer output in 2026, rising to 86% in 2027, squeezing out smartphone and consumer electronics production.
key_facts.excerpt: AI wafers are expected to account for around 86 percent of N3 capacity by 2027. Weakening smartphone demand is freeing up capacity that gets redirected straight to AI chips.

key_facts.fact: Nvidia, Google, Amazon, and AMD are all moving their AI accelerators to TSMC's N3 process simultaneously in 2026, creating a demand shock the foundry is unprepared for.
key_facts.excerpt: In 2026, Nvidia, Google, Amazon, and AMD are all moving their AI accelerators to TSMC's N3 process at the same time. According to SemiAnalysis, TSMC has underestimated demand for years and won't be able to build enough capacity for at least two more years.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic added a staggering $6 billion of ARR in the single month of February alone, driven by Claude Code, and would have added more if compute were available.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic added a staggering $6B of ARR in the single month of February alone driven by broad adoption of agentic coding platform Claude Code, and if Anthropic had more compute they would have added more.

key_facts.fact: HBM consumes roughly three times more wafer capacity per bit than standard DRAM, and with HBM4 that ratio gets even worse.
key_facts.excerpt: Memory is also scarce. HBM consumes roughly three times more wafer capacity per bit than standard DRAM, and with HBM4 that ratio gets even worse.

key_facts.fact: Dylan Patel of SemiAnalysis identifies three key bottlenecks to scaling AI compute: logic (N3 wafers), memory (HBM), and power, noting that H100 GPUs are worth more today than when they launched 3 years ago.
key_facts.excerpt: Dylan Patel, founder of SemiAnalysis, provides a deep dive into the 3 big bottlenecks to scaling AI compute: logic, memory, and power.

key_facts.fact: Reallocating 25% of smartphone N3 wafers could enable production of roughly 700,000 additional Rubin GPUs or 1.5 million additional TPU v7s.
key_facts.excerpt: AI accelerators will consume nearly 60% of TSMC's total N3 wafer output in 2026, rising to 86% in 2027, effectively squeezing out smartphone and consumer electronics production.

stories.headline: ByteDance suspends Seedance 2.0 global launch after Hollywood copyright disputes

key_facts.fact: ByteDance has put on hold the planned mid-March global launch of its AI video-generation model Seedance 2.0 after copyright disputes with major Hollywood studios and streaming platforms.
key_facts.excerpt: TikTok's Chinese parent, ByteDance, has put on hold the global launch of its latest video-generation model, Seedance 2.0, after copyright disputes with major Hollywood studios and streaming platforms.

key_facts.fact: Five major studios and the Motion Picture Association filed cease-and-desist letters: Disney, Warner Bros. Discovery, Paramount, Netflix, and Sony Pictures.
key_facts.excerpt: ByteDance has suspended the planned global rollout of Seedance 2.0 after five major studios and the Motion Picture Association fired cease-and-desist letters over copyright infringement.

key_facts.fact: Disney alleged ByteDance packaged the model with 'a pirated library of Disney's copyrighted characters from Star Wars, Marvel, and other Disney franchises.'
key_facts.excerpt: Disney accused ByteDance of stocking its Seedance 2.0 'with a pirated library of Disney's copyrighted characters.'

key_facts.fact: The MPA stated 'the scale and consistency of these results demonstrate systemic infringement rather than inadvertence,' calling the violation 'a feature, not a bug.'
key_facts.excerpt: The MPA stated 'the scale and consistency of these results demonstrate systemic infringement rather than inadvertence.'

key_facts.fact: Seedance 2.0 was launched in China on February 12, 2026 as a multimodal model accepting text, images, audio, and video to generate cinematic-quality footage.
key_facts.excerpt: ByteDance officially launched Seedance 2.0 in China on February 12, 2026. The multimodal model accepts text, images, audio, and video as inputs and generates cinematic quality footage.

stories.headline: Nvidia GTC 2026 to showcase CPU pivot and Groq LPU integration for agentic AI

key_facts.fact: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang will keynote GTC starting March 16, expected to unveil Vera CPU — an 88-core custom Arm processor with simultaneous multithreading and confidential computing — with Meta as its first major datacenter-scale deployment.
key_facts.excerpt: An 88-core custom Arm processor featuring simultaneous multithreading and confidential computing capabilities. Meta will reportedly deploy Vera at datacenter scale.

key_facts.fact: Nvidia acquired Groq's IP and talent for $20 billion in December 2025 and plans to combine GPU technology with Groq's dataflow architecture to address token generation bottlenecks in agentic AI inference.
key_facts.excerpt: Nvidia acquired Groq's intellectual property and talent for $20 billion in December 2025. The company plans to combine its GPU technology with Groq's dataflow architecture to address token generation bottlenecks.

key_facts.fact: Groq's SRAM-heavy architecture can achieve 500+ tokens per second, vastly outpacing traditional GPU approaches for latency-sensitive agentic inference workloads.
key_facts.excerpt: SRAM-heavy architectures like Groq can achieve 500+ tokens per second, vastly outpacing traditional GPU approaches for latency-sensitive inference.

key_facts.fact: Both Nvidia and AMD are seeing unprecedented demand for CPUs as AI workloads shift from training to reasoning-intensive agentic applications, representing a fundamental architectural shift.
key_facts.excerpt: AI industry shifts focus to CPUs as agentic systems demand orchestration, making CPUs the new bottleneck in workflows.

key_facts.fact: Jensen Huang reportedly considers OpenClaw 'the most important software release probably ever'; Nvidia is developing NemoClaw as a proprietary safety-focused alternative.
key_facts.excerpt: Jensen Huang reportedly considers OpenClaw 'the most important software release probably ever,' despite known security vulnerabilities. Nvidia is developing NemoClaw, a proprietary safety-focused alternative.

key_facts.fact: Rubin GPUs feature up to 288 GB of HBM4 memory with 22 TB/s bandwidth and 35-50 petaFLOPS, with Kyber Racks (2027) targeting 144 GPU sockets at 600 kW and Feynman GPUs (2028) exceeding 1 megawatt per rack.
key_facts.excerpt: Rubin delivers up to 288 GB of HBM4 memory with 22 TB/s bandwidth, 35-50 petaFLOPS of NVFP4 performance. Kyber Racks (2027): 144 GPU sockets with 600 kW power draw. Feynman GPUs (2028): Expected to exceed 1 megawatt per rack.

stories.headline: Humanity's Last Exam published in Nature: frontier AI scores only 40-50% on expert test

key_facts.fact: Nearly 1,000 experts from over 50 countries created a 2,500-question benchmark spanning 100+ subjects including mathematics, humanities, natural sciences, and ancient languages.
key_facts.excerpt: Nearly 1,000 experts from more than 50 countries collaborated to build a new assessment called Humanity's Last Exam, or HLE, a 2,500-question test covering more than 100 subjects.

key_facts.fact: GPT-4o scored 2.7%, Claude 3.5 Sonnet 4.1%, OpenAI's o1 about 8%, while Gemini 3.1 Pro and Claude Opus 4.6 reached 40-50% accuracy — still far below expert human performance.
key_facts.excerpt: GPT-4o scored 2.7%, Claude 3.5 Sonnet 4.1%, and OpenAI's o1 model reached about 8% accuracy. More recent systems, such as Gemini 3.1 Pro and Claude Opus 4.6, improved to around 40-50% accuracy.

key_facts.fact: Questions were deliberately designed so any question correctly answered by current AI models at the time was removed, ensuring the exam measures genuine capability gaps.
key_facts.excerpt: Every question was tested against leading AI models. Any question correctly answered by current AI was removed.

key_facts.fact: The study was published in Nature and led by Texas A&M's Dr. Tung Nguyen, who stated: 'intelligence isn't just about pattern recognition — it's about depth, context and specialized expertise.'
key_facts.excerpt: Dr. Nguyen stated: 'When AI systems start performing extremely well on human benchmarks, it's tempting to think they're approaching human-level understanding. But HLE reminds us that intelligence isn't just about pattern recognition — it's about depth, context and specialized expertise.'

key_facts.fact: The benchmark is publicly available at lastexam.ai and is published in Nature (2026; 649(8099): 1139) as a permanent measurement tool for tracking AI progress against the expert human frontier.
key_facts.excerpt: To inform research and policymaking upon a clear understanding of model capabilities, we publicly release HLE at https://lastexam.ai.

stories.headline: Microsoft launches Copilot Health, its most direct consumer health AI entry

key_facts.fact: Microsoft launched Copilot Health, a dedicated space within its Copilot AI assistant that aggregates personal health data from wearables, electronic health records, and lab results to surface a 'coherent story' of a user's health.
key_facts.excerpt: Microsoft has launched Copilot Health, a dedicated, secure space within its Copilot AI assistant that aggregates personal health data from wearables, electronic health records, and laboratory results, then applies AI to surface what the company calls a 'coherent story' of a user's health.

key_facts.fact: The product opened its waitlist on March 12, 2026 and is rolling out in phases, initially to English-speaking adults in the United States.
key_facts.excerpt: The product opened its waitlist on 12 March 2026 and is rolling out in phases, initially to English-speaking adults in the United States.

key_facts.fact: The launch places Microsoft alongside OpenAI (ChatGPT Health, January 2026) and Anthropic (Claude for Healthcare, January 2026), marking a convergence of all three major AI platforms into consumer health.
key_facts.excerpt: The launch marks Microsoft's most direct entry into consumer health AI and places it alongside OpenAI, which introduced ChatGPT Health in January 2026, and Anthropic, which unveiled Claude for Healthcare the same month.

key_facts.fact: Dominic King, VP of Health at Microsoft AI, stated: '2026 feels like an important year for consumer health.'
key_facts.excerpt: In the words of Dominic King, VP of Health at Microsoft AI: '2026 feels like an important year for consumer health.'
